Cc: procurement@licenta.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing exhibit — packaging carveouts and minimum commit question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput numbers and the routing controls. We're trying to finalize internal budget language and Legal is asking for tighter wording in the pricing exhibit around the 'minimum commitment hurdle' and packaging carveouts. A few concrete asks:

- Can Redwood clarify if committed minimums are measured on billed tokens or on requested tokens (we need billed tokens for our accounting).
- The order schedule refers to "packaged SKUs" but doesn't define whether legacy invoices should be pro-rated if we migrate subsets of traffic mid-term.
- We'd like a temporary ramp carveout for months 1–3 if adoption lags.

I've attached our suggested markup (we reviewed vendor redlines) and would appreciate a proposed clause from your side that preserves Redwood's unit economics while giving us predictable accounting treatment.

If it's easier, happy to hop on a short call later today.

Thanks,
Alice Jensen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Licenta Health

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — packaging carveouts and minimum commit question

Thanks Alice — quick answers up front, then a proposed approach: 

1) Measurement: Redwood measures the "Committed Usage" for minimums on billed tokens (post-currency/usage calculation) for clarity in invoicing. We'll reflect that explicitly.

2) SKU migration / pro-ration: We propose a pro-rata protocol in Appendix A that treats an SKUs migration window as a transition period; if a customer migrates N% of traffic mid-term, the Order Schedule will true-up billed quantities on a pro-rata basis for the relevant invoice period rather than reclassifying the entire month. That preserves revenue recognition on both sides.

3) Ramp carveout: We can offer a 90-day soft-ramp where the minimum commit counts against a reduced "onboarding baseline" (50% of negotiated minimum for months 1–3) provided the customer engages with Redwood's onboarding playbook and weekly adoption checkpoints. After month 3 the baseline steps up to the contracted minimum with a one-time true-up over the following invoice.

I attached a short markup of the exhibit that inserts definitions ("Committed Usage", "Packaged SKU", "Transition Window") and a sample true-up formula. Two things we need from Licenta to finalize: (a) confirmation you measure on-billed tokens for your internal accounting (so both sides align), and (b) whether the onboarding checkpoints are acceptable (we typically run a 6-week adoption cadence but can formalize a 90-day schedule for this deal).

[Attachment: OrderSchedule_AppendixA.xlsx (xlsx)]

—Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@licenta.com>

Karthik / Marissa — thanks, those answers help a lot. A few follow-ups from our Finance and Legal: 

- Finance confirms we recognize on billed tokens; please add a short sample calculation in the appendix for how billed tokens are derived from raw request tokens plus any adjustments.
- Legal asked to soften the one-time true-up language so there is a 30-day notice and split-collection window (we proposed spread over the next two invoices). They also asked for a cap on onboarding credits not to exceed 15% of the first-quarter invoice.
- Regarding the transition window: can you include an explicit example (line items) of pro-ration when a packaged SKU is deprecated and partially replaced mid-month? That will expedite internal approvals.

If you can accept the 30-day notice + two-invoice spread and the onboarding credit cap, we can advance to signature and route to our procurement committee tomorrow.

Alice Jensen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Licenta Health
